positioning: Ashish Srivastava — vCISO advisory, security transformation and AI assurance
service_boundary: Proposed services and scoped delivery targets. Client outcomes are established through separately agreed engagement evidence.

pillars.title: Keep the business running
pillars.promise: Know which services matter most, where they can fail and whether recovery actually works.
outputs: Restore test with observed recovery gaps
pillars.measure: Measured restore time and data loss against agreed service objectives.
pillars.decision: Which service must recover first, and who can authorize that recovery?
problems: Critical operations stop
Prioritize essential services, dependency failures and continuity decisions.
Ransomware and cyber extortion
Review attack paths, containment choices, restoration and crisis ownership.
The business cannot recover
Exercise restoration and record missing dependencies, data loss and failed attempts.
Cyber or AI failure threatens physical safety
Work with process and safety owners on operating boundaries and escalation.
Security operations cannot respond effectively
Test detection, escalation, communications and response authority.

pillars.title: Protect customers, funds and IP
pillars.promise: Connect identity, transaction authority and application controls to the information and money at risk.
outputs: Authorized application tests and remediation evidence
pillars.measure: Priority access paths tested, excessive privileges removed and findings retested.
pillars.decision: Who may see this record or authorize this transaction, and what blocks misuse?
problems: Cyber fraud and executive impersonation
Review independent verification and high-risk transaction approvals.
Customer or regulated information is exposed
Trace sensitive data, access boundaries, disclosure and response obligations.
Trade secrets or proprietary AI are stolen
Define ownership and access controls for code, models and proprietary data.
Human and machine identities have excessive access
Review human, service and agent privileges, revocation and emergency access.
Unknown assets and legacy weaknesses remain unmanaged
Inventory the scoped estate and prioritize exposure with service owners.

pillars.title: Deploy AI with accountable control
pillars.promise: Make AI use cases, data boundaries and agent permissions reviewable before they become business authority.
outputs: AI inventory, risk tiers and accountable owners
Model, retrieval and tool threat model
Evaluation, approval, monitoring and rollback gates
pillars.measure: Scoped use cases reviewed, allowed/denied cases exercised and unresolved risks assigned.
pillars.decision: What can the AI access or do, and which decision must stay with a person?
problems: AI deployment creates regulatory exposure
Establish use-case applicability, accountable review and supporting evidence.
AI agents act beyond their authority
Restrict tool actions, identities and data reach; define approval and revocation.
Shadow AI and unknown agents
Identify AI use within the agreed estate and define an admission process.
AI applications can be manipulated
Exercise prompt, retrieval, output and tool boundaries in authorized tests.
Models or datasets are compromised
Review model/data provenance, component admission and change control.
AI produces unreliable business decisions
Set task-specific evaluation and human review for consequential outputs.
AI harms customers or employees
Define impact, fairness and safety evaluation with accountable domain owners.
AI decisions lack accountability
Assign owners, trace actions and establish review and challenge routes.
AI becomes unsafe or unreliable after deployment
Define monitoring, re-evaluation triggers, rollback and stop criteria.
AI use violates privacy or intellectual-property rights
Review data provenance, rights, confidentiality and legal applicability.
AI-generated software introduces weaknesses
Apply secure design, dependency review and meaningful regression checks.

pillars.title: Reduce dependency surprises
pillars.promise: Make critical suppliers, shared dependencies and exit constraints visible to the people accepting the risk.
outputs: Critical supplier and upstream dependency map
Continuity, concentration and exit decision brief
pillars.measure: Critical dependencies with owners, reviewed evidence and tested or documented alternatives.
pillars.decision: Which shared supplier failure can stop the service, and what is our fallback?
problems: A critical supplier fails
Identify continuity options and ownership for high-impact dependencies.
Vendor risk is poorly understood or monitored
Tie assurance requests, contracts and review cadence to supplier criticality.
Hidden suppliers create common points of failure
Map material upstream dependencies and concentration assumptions.
Supplier financial or geopolitical exposure threatens delivery
Escalate ownership, jurisdiction and continuity questions with specialist input.
Software and hardware supply chains cannot be trusted
Review provenance, approved components, signed admission and lifecycle support.

pillars.title: Retain control of critical technology
pillars.promise: Define sovereignty across data, operators, keys, suppliers and recovery—not just the location of a workload.
outputs: Key-custody, exit and post-quantum dependency plan
pillars.measure: Critical external dependencies identified and agreed local-operation boundaries exercised.
pillars.decision: Who can operate, decrypt, update, support and recover the service?
problems: The business lacks control over data and technology
Review jurisdiction, operator authority, key custody, portability and recovery.

pillars.title: Make risk and investment explainable
pillars.promise: Turn fragmented security activity into owned decisions, an investment case and evidence leadership can challenge.
outputs: Board risk brief and accountable risk register
Costed options and a prioritized 90-day roadmap
pillars.measure: Priority risks with owners, explicit assumptions, funded decisions and dated evidence.
pillars.decision: Which business loss are we treating, why this investment and what will show progress?
problems: Leadership cannot see total enterprise risk
Connect service impact, dependencies, risk appetite and treatment decisions.
Security spending lacks demonstrable value
Compare treatment options, costs and loss assumptions; test control effectiveness.
AI investment fails to produce financial returns
Define business-value hypotheses and stage gates before further investment.
